subject.title: contextPruning (mode: cache-ttl) never fires on OpenAI models: isCacheTtlEligibleProvider excludes OpenAI, so the idle-gap tool-result firebreak is dead for the highest-volume provider

question: Should native OpenAI cache-TTL pruning be enabled through the existing eligibility gate, or should this wait for provider-agnostic or retention-aware pruning semantics?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but enabling OpenAI changes retained context behavior for existing configurations and needs maintainer intent before the linked PR can safely land.

options.title: Prove and approve OpenAI TTL behavior
options.body: Keep the linked PR as the fix path, but require explicit maintainer-approved OpenAI semantics plus redacted native idle-gap proof before merge.

options.title: Switch to provider-agnostic pruning
options.body: Reject the provider eligibility widening and pursue a pruning mode that does not depend on prompt-cache eligibility.

options.title: Defer OpenAI pruning
options.body: Document native OpenAI as unsupported for cache-TTL pruning for now and leave broader cache/pruning design to a later product decision.

recommendation.title: Prove and approve OpenAI TTL behavior
recommendation.body: Keep the linked PR as the fix path, but require explicit maintainer-approved OpenAI semantics plus redacted native idle-gap proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The current cache-TTL code and recent provider eligibility refactors point to this area owner, while the decision can pull in adjacent provider/runtime reviewers as needed.
